why: Most people will not clone and run a project just to see what it looks like. A live link and a couple of screenshots show them in ten seconds whether it fits their needs.
question: What does it look like, and can I try it right now?
questionNote: Right after the title and summary
who: Required for portfolios; web apps need at least one
whoNote: Backend APIs link to API docs instead

parts.heading: ## Demo
parts.text: If the project is deployed, link to it here. Make the link text say where it goes, such as "Corner Breakfast live demo", instead of "Click here".

parts.heading: ## Screenshots
parts.text: Include one to three screenshots of key screens, stored in the repository and linked with relative paths. Give every image descriptive alt text in brackets and a short caption below.
parts.emphasis: Never leave placeholder images such as fakeimg.pl, and do not use a file name or "screenshot" as alt text.

parts.heading: Test account
parts.text: If login is required to see the screens, provide a read-only test account as a normal list rather than inside a command block.

notes.title: Link says "click here"
notes.text: Say where the link goes, not just "click here".

notes.title: Alt text says "screenshot"
notes.text: Describe what the screen shows, not the filename.

notes.title: Uses a placeholder image
notes.text: Replace stand-in URLs with real screenshots in the repo.

notes.title: Only images without text
notes.text: Add a sentence below explaining what the screen does.

lines: Tap any item in a category to add it to the cart.
Adjust quantities and pick a time before ordering.

tip.title: Store screenshots in the repository, not on image hosts
paragraphs: Put screenshots in a folder like docs/images/ and reference them with relative paths. Links pasted from chat apps or external image hosts often expire after a few months and leave broken images.
One or two screenshots of the main screens are enough; too many force readers to scroll a long way before reaching the setup steps.

types.web-app: If the app requires login, include a read-only test account so visitors can look around safely.
types.course-example: Show one screenshot of the finished result so students can check whether their version looks right.
types.portfolio: This is the most important block for a portfolio. Make sure the live link works, and include a mobile view if you built one.
types.backend-api: Usually there are no screens; use the heading "## API Documentation" instead and link to the local and online docs.
